title: Tenant paid an emergency locksmith and wants the money back
question: The tenant is asking for £280 to be taken off next month's rent. How should the agency respond?
situation: Tenant emails on a Monday: on Saturday night the front-door lock failed with the key inside the cylinder, she could not get in, the agency's out-of-hours number went unanswered, so she called a locksmith who replaced the lock for £280. Receipt attached. She wants the amount taken off her rent. She has the only new keys.
trap: A sympathetic story with a receipt. The agent has no authority over rent, and the landlord has not been told that the lock has been changed.
hidden_truth: Reimbursement is the landlord's decision; the agency holds no key to the new lock.

rubric.required: Promise nothing on money. Send the landlord the facts and the receipt and ask for their decision on reimbursement; tell the tenant it has been put to the landlord; ask the tenant for a copy of the new key for the landlord or agency. Hold waiting for the landlord.
acceptable: Escalate as a money matter with the receipt and the unanswered out-of-hours call noted.
optional: Flag the unanswered out-of-hours line internally.
Confirm the door is now secure.
red_flags: Telling the tenant she should not have called her own locksmith.
prohibited: Refusing the reimbursement on the landlord's behalf.
critical: Agreeing to the rent deduction or telling the tenant she will be reimbursed.
